claim.summary: For a real polynomial p of degree at least one and p_t = exp(-t D^2) p, the largest imaginary part M(t) of a zero of p_t satisfies M(t)^2 <= max(0, M(0)^2 - 2t) for t >= 0; real-rootedness persists; and at a simple zero x + iy with y > 0, d(y^2)/dt = -2 - 4y times the sum of (y - y_j)/|z - z_j|^2 over the zeros other than it and its conjugate.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof from the zero dynamics z_k' = 2 sum 1/(z_k - z_j). The polynomial case of a contraction attributed from memory to de Bruijn, whose paper is unread; taken to be classical. Used to state the heat flow as a filter on methods: a property that H_0 shares with a backward-flowed function cannot be the only one a proof uses (by the main theorem of arXiv 1801.05914, read). Which recorded premises are of that kind is not decided.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: First development of the queued heat-flow item: the polynomial contraction with its rate, and the filter in a form that survives review.
significance.next_action: Decide for each recorded prime-side premise whether it uses multiplicativity or only a sum over n that persists under the flow; prove the absorption rate for a finite configuration.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry; no new computation (a saved test of the second review agrees).

significance.note: Context: a classical fact in its polynomial case. Novelty not claimed.

claim.summary: For continuous even real g of compact support with phi(s) = Re h(s + i/2) >= 0, h the transform of g: Re h(t+iy) = (1/2pi) int phi(s) K_y(t-s) ds with K_y(t) = 2 pi cos(pi y) cosh(pi t)/(sinh^2(pi t) + cos^2(pi y)); hence Re h(gamma + iy) >= cos(pi y) cos(pi delta) exp(-pi |gamma - gamma0|) Re h(gamma0 + i delta) in the open strip; and if the sum of Re h over a multiset Z of points of the strip is at most B while c Re h(gamma0 + i delta) > B, then cos(pi delta) sum over Z of cos(pi y_rho) exp(-pi |gamma_rho - gamma0|) < c.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof (Fourier inversion, an explicit Poisson kernel of the strip, Harnack with constants), with a numerical control of the kernel and of the inequality. Limits explicit-formula certificates that require nonnegativity on the whole critical strip: they can exclude a point at distance delta from the line only where the weighted count of actual zeros near its height is below 4/cos(pi delta). The size of that count for zeta is recalled, not derived. Believed classical; no novelty claimed.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Answers the second route review's decisive test: positivity on the whole strip cannot separate a point from the zeros near it, so that formulation reproduces at best the classical region where the zeros nearby are on the line.
significance.next_action: Decide what a certificate needs when positivity is required only outside a window around the height.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry; one recalled integral checked numerically to 1.8e-10.

significance.note: Context: an obstruction to a method, elementary. Novelty not claimed.

relationships.note: The model's negative direction for the Gram form used positivity on the line only; this lemma shows the price of positivity on the strip. Positivity relaxed in a window with a count; an averaged weighted count of zeros: new relationship with lem:relaxed-positivity-obstruction. De Bruijn's contraction for real polynomials under the backward heat equation: new relationship with lem:polynomial-strip-contraction.

relationships.scope: The item proposed that lemma's class as the first premise to test; the obstruction holds for every configuration and is indifferent to the flow.
